  - text: CLASS 10 · CIRCLE PROOFS
  - heading "Tangent Perpendicular to Radius" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Understand why a tangent at a point on a circle is perpendicular to the radius through that point.
  - text: 30 min RIGOROUS PROOF geometry2d
  - navigation:
    - button "Interact"
    - button "Learn"
    - button "Example"
    - button "Formula"
    - button "Practice"
  - main:
    - heading "INTERACTIVE EXPLORATION" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Drag point T on the circle and rotate line ℓ. Observe and discover.
    - complementary:
      - heading "1 Drag tangent point T" [level=3]
      - text: Move T on the circle
      - slider "Tangent point angle": "270"
      - paragraph: T angle 270°
      - heading "2 Rotate line ℓ" [level=3]
      - text: Rotate the purple line
      - slider "Tangent line angle": "0"
      - paragraph: Angle of ℓ 0°
      - heading "Display options" [level=3]
      - text: Show radius OT
      - checkbox "Show radius OT ON" [checked]
      - text: ON Show shortest distance
      - checkbox "Show shortest distance ON" [checked]
      - text: ON Show angle ∠OTℓ
      - checkbox "Show angle ∠OTℓ ON" [checked]
      - text: ON Snap to perpendicular
      - checkbox "Snap to perpendicular ON" [checked]
      - text: "ON"
      - heading "Comparison mode" [level=3]
      - button "Tangent"
      - button "Secant"
      - button "None"
      - button "Reset":
        - img
        - text: Reset
    - article:
      - img "Tangent line and radius interactive diagram":
        - text: Chord Tangent Angle O
        - slider "Tangent point T"
        - text: T
        - slider "Rotate tangent line"
        - text: OT = 6.00 90.0° ℓ
      - paragraph: Drag T or rotate ℓ until the line just touches the circle at T. The radius OT will be perpendicular to ℓ.
    - complementary:
      - 'heading "STATUS: TANGENT" [level=3]'
      - paragraph: "Intersections: 1"
      - paragraph: "Distance d(O,ℓ): 6.00"
      - paragraph: "∠OTℓ: 90.0°"
      - strong:
        - img
        - text: Perpendicular
    - article:
      - heading "WHY IT WORKS" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Among all lines through T, the radius OT is the shortest distance from O to a tangent line.
      - paragraph: A shortest distance is perpendicular to that line. Therefore the tangent at T is perpendicular to OT.
      - text: O T
      - strong: d(O,ℓ) = OT = 6.00 (minimum)
    - article:
      - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: "Given: Circle O with radius 6 units. If OT is vertical and ℓ is tangent at T:"
      - list:
        - listitem: OT is a radius, so OT = 6.
        - listitem: A tangent at T is perpendicular to OT.
      - text: O T
      - strong: "Result: ℓ is horizontal and ∠OTℓ = 90°."
    - article:
      - heading "A COMMON MISCONCEPTION" [level=2]:
        - img
        - text: A COMMON MISCONCEPTION
      - paragraph: A line that looks like it touches the circle may actually be a secant.
      - paragraph: A secant intersects the circle at two points, so it is not the tangent.
      - text: O A B
      - strong: This line is a secant, not a tangent.
    - heading "YOUR CHALLENGE" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Rotate ℓ until it is tangent to the circle at T and verify the angle.
    - heading "Tasks" [level=3]
    - paragraph: 1 Set the line so there is exactly one intersection.
    - paragraph: 2 The shortest distance from O to ℓ equals OT.
    - paragraph: 3 The angle ∠OTℓ must be 90°.
    - text: O T ℓ
    - heading "Live checks" [level=3]
    - paragraph:

      - img

      - img
    - paragraph:

      - img
    - strong:
      - img
      - text: Well done! ℓ is tangent at T.
    - paragraph: "Tip: Enable “Snap to perpendicular” to lock ℓ at exactly 90°."
